titulek: Norway strengthens border surveillance system to detect drones near Russia
titulekPuvodni: Norway strengthens border surveillance system to detect drones near Russia
shrnuti: Norway is deploying NASAMS sensors in Kirkenes and reinforcing its military presence with over 30 soldiers to detect drones near the Russian border.

vyrez.text:
Norway deploys drone detection system near Russian border | Ukrainska Pravda
The Norwegian flag. Photo: Getty Images
The Norwegian Armed Forces are deploying an aerial surveillance system in the town of Kirkenes, near the Russian border, to detect drones that stray off course at an early stage.
Source: a press release by the Norwegian government, as reported by European Pravda
Details: The Norwegian Air Force is deploying specialised NASAMS sensors, while the military garrison in the region will be reinforced by more than 30 soldiers.
Advertisement:





"We have seen in other countries that drones can go astray. This is something Norway takes seriously. We must be prepared, even though we do not currently see an increased aerial threat to Norway or the population of Finnmark," said Norwegian Defence Minister Tore O. Sandvik.
The government noted that the measures are preventive and are not linked to any specific new threat.
The sensors are designed to detect drones, warn of their presence and provide a comprehensive picture of all activity in the airspace over border areas.

shrnuti: Latvia issued an air-raid warning in two eastern municipalities overnight after an unidentified drone entered its airspace and crashed near the Russian border.

Aircraft. Stock photo: MIL.LV/LV
An air-raid warning was issued in Latvia's Ludza and Balvi municipalities on the night of 2-3 November after an unidentified drone was detected. The object crashed in the Balvi area.
Source: European Pravda, citing the Latvian National Armed Forces
Details: An air-raid warning was issued in the Ludza and Balvi municipalities at 00:10 on 2 November. Fighter jets from NATO's Baltic Air Defence mission were deployed in the airspace over the Baltic states. In response to the threat, the Latvian Armed Forces also deployed interceptor drones.

The Latvian National Armed Forces urged members of the public not to approach or touch any suspicious objects or debris they might find and to call the emergency number 112 immediately.

shrnuti: Latvia has activated an orange alert in eastern districts and deploys a Blaze interceptor drone after an unidentified UAV breaches its airspace.

Latvia on map. Photo: google.maps
The Latvian Armed Forces have deployed a drone interceptor after an unidentified unmanned aerial vehicle breached Latvian airspace on the evening of 1 November.
Source: European Pravda , citing Latvian media outlet LSM
Details: An
orange alert
An orange alert in Latvia refers to a high-level warning issued by authorities either for airspace threats (such as detected drones or aircraft) or for severe weather conditions (such as violent thunderstorms and heavy hail)
was declared in the Krāslava and Ludza districts of Latvia after an unidentified drone violated the nation's airspace at 18:59 on Sunday.
Advertisement:





Seventeen minutes later, the flying object exited Latvian airspace, crossing back over the Latvian-Russian border.
The Latvian military reacted to the detected threat to its airspace by launching a Blaze interceptor drone. At 19:19, the decision was taken to activate the interceptor's self-destruct mechanism to prevent any potential risk of violating the state border with Russia.

titulekPuvodni: Romania scrambles four fighter jets due to drone incursion
shrnuti: Romania sent four F-16s and a helicopter after two drones entered its airspace on 31 October, triggering alerts in six counties; no crashes reported.

vyrez.text:
Romania scrambles four F-16s after two drones violate its airspace | Ukrainska Pravda
A fighter jet. Stock photo: Getty Images
Radar surveillance systems operated by Romania's Ministry of National Defence detected two unmanned aerial vehicles that had entered the country's airspace without authorisation on the evening of 31 October.
Source: Romania's Ministry of National Defence , as reported by European Pravda
Details: Romania scrambled four F-16 fighter jets and an IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter to monitor the situation and manage the response after two unmanned aerial vehicles violated the country's airspace.
Advertisement:





Alerts were issued in six Romanian counties due to the airspace violation: Iași, Neamț, Vaslui, Botoșani, Bacău and Suceava.
One of the two drones left the country's airspace, while the other was last spotted in the area between the counties of Vaslui and Bacău.
No drone crashes were reported.
Background:
On the same day, a drone violated Moldovan airspace during Russian aerial attacks on Ukraine.
On 23 October, Moldova's Foreign Ministry condemned the violation of the country's airspace by a drone and blamed Russia for the incident.

Bombariasztás miatt kényszerleszállást hajtott végre kedd délelőtt a Varsó melletti Modlin repülőtéren egy Londonból elindult járat. Az utasokat kimenekítették, a repülőteret lezárták – közölte kedden a lengyel TVN24.
A Boeing 737 MAX típusú gép eredetileg a varsói Chopin központi repülőtérre tartott. A reptér szóvivőjének közlése szerint a gép fedélzetén 181 ember tartózkodott. In Luxembourg and Belgium, several Delhaize stores were affected. The company says shops are still open and the food is safe. Carrefour in Belgium says 15 of its 700 stores were hit, with some fridges soaring in temperature. A similar attack hit supermarkets in France on 12 October.

Nach der Landung wurde das Flugzeug von von Behörden untersucht.








Ein Flugzeug der ungarischen Billigairline Wizz Air ist wegen einer Bombendrohung nach Budapest umgeleitet worden. Die Maschine sei auf dem Weg von London in die bulgarische Hauptstadt Sofia gewesen, teilte der ungarische Verteidigungsminister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi am Montag auf Facebook mit. Ein ungarischer Gripen-Kampfjet sei aufgestiegen, um das Passagierflugzeug nach Budapest zu eskortieren. Es sei sicher in der ungarischen Hauptstadt gelandet.

Source: Astra
Ukrainian drones struck Russia’s Samara region overnight on November 2. Regional authorities had not officially commented on the strikes by the time of publication, but Samara’s airport suspended operations for two hours because of the drone threat.
Ukrainian monitoring channels and Astra, an independent Telegram channel, cited photos and videos from eyewitnesses in reporting that the drones, according to preliminary reports, struck the Samara Linear Production and Dispatch Station (LPDS) near the settlement of Prosvet.
The Samara LPDS is the largest tank farm in Europe, part of a network operated by Transneft. Four pipelines carrying oil from Western Siberia, Tatarstan, the Orenburg region, and Kazakhstan connect to the station.
Ukrainian military drones struck the Samara LPDS several times in October, causing fires and damaging storage tanks.

Poland's president called urgent crisis talks with party representatives on Saturday after a dramatic showdown at the country's constitutional court between the centrist government and nationalist right.
Karol Nawrocki cut short a trip to Senegal and returned to Warsaw, where police had surrounded the court on Friday following the suspension of its president Bogdan Swieczkowski.
He said the talks were necessary because of "the threat to internal security", in a statement read on his behalf outside court the next morning.
The nationalist president also denounced what he called a "violation of the constitutional order" and demanded police withdraw from the court. Talks were due to begin at 1:00 pm local time (1200 GMT) at the presidential palace.
